items.title: Being universally closed is fpqc local on the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that universal closedness is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 5731-5735). The proof records base-change stability and Zariski locality, then treats a flat surjective morphism of affines S' -> S with universally closed base change f': for an arbitrary T -> S the two cartesian squares of the displayed diagram reduce the assumption to closedness of the middle vertical arrow; the right horizontal arrows are flat, quasi-compact and surjective as base changes of S' -> S, so a subset of T is closed exactly when its inverse image in S' x_S T is closed, by the fpqc quotient-topology lemma; a diagram chase then gives closedness of T x_S X -> T, i.e. universal closedness of f, and the general lemma on fpqc locality concludes (proof lines 5737-5769). The level is H3: the reduction to the quotient topology criterion is displayed and the chase is carried out on an explicit diagram.
